answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the inlet hash is checked against the hollow checkpoint at intake, the voyage audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 145 aliases cost 394 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
